issues.legal_issue: A civil court lacks jurisdiction over a suit seeking a declaration of ownership and possession when deciding the claim requires determining whether the land is shamlat deh vested in a Panchayat.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a representative civil suit seeking a declaration that they owned and possessed the land, that the Panchayat had no right in it, and that revenue-record entries showing the Panchayat as entitled to it were incorrect, together with an injunction.
The Panchayat, which was a defendant, claimed that the land was shamlat deh and had vested in it.
Granting the requested declaration required deciding whether the land was shamlat deh and whether it belonged to the Panchayat.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not maintainable in the civil court because the question whether the land was shamlat deh vested in the Panchayat had to be decided by the Collector under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 11–13 of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, as amended, assign to the Collector claims concerning rights, title or interests in land vested or alleged not to be vested in a Panchayat; provide an appeal to the Commissioner and finality for the resulting orders; and bar civil courts from deciding whether property or an interest in it is shamlat deh vested or deemed vested in a Panchayat, or matters the Collector or Commissioner is empowered to determine. A plaintiff cannot confer civil jurisdiction by framing a claim to avoid expressly seeking a declaration that land is not shamlat deh when the court must decide that question to grant relief. Bhagu v. Ram Sarup was distinguished because the plaintiff there sought an injunction concerning use of a street, did not claim ownership or deny the Panchayat’s ownership, and the Panchayat was not a defendant.

predicates.civil_suit_for_ownership_or_possession: The proceeding is a civil suit in which the plaintiff seeks a declaration of ownership or possession of land.
predicates.panchayat_claims_vested_shamlat_land: The Panchayat, as a defendant, claims that the disputed land is shamlat land vested in it.
predicates.deciding_relief_requires_classifying_lan: The court would have to determine whether the land is shamlat land or is vested in the Panchayat to decide the relief sought.
predicates.civil_court_lacks_jurisdiction: The civil court cannot entertain or decide the suit.

issues.definition: When a civil suit seeks ownership or possession, the Panchayat claims the land as vested shamlat land, and deciding the relief requires classifying the land or determining vesting, the civil court cannot decide the suit.
